subject: High 5xx rate from sentinel2b in production (us-west-2)
messages:
From: Evelyn Harper <evelyn@lumentech.com>

Date: 2026-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High 5xx rate from sentinel2b in production (us-west-2)

Hi Jasmine,

We're seeing a spike in 5xx responses and timeouts from the /v1/generate endpoint using model sentinel2b in our us-west-2 region starting around 08:55 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~8% and latency for affected calls is 2-3x. Examples: request ids 0x9f3a4, 0x9f3a7. We're routing traffic through your hosted API (api.redwood.com) with api key tied to LumenTech.

Impact: autocomplete and smart-suggest features are experiencing timeouts; several customers have reported failed flows.

I've attached a small snapshot of our request logs (ops_snapshot_0907.json) and relevant traces. Can you confirm whether this is a known degradation on your side and ETA for mitigation?

Thanks,
Evelyn Harper
Head of Platform Operations, LumenTech
Evelyn.Harper@lumentech.com

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the log snapshot. I've kicked off triage with SRE and Support. Looping in Ben (Support) and Markus (SRE) to lead the technical investigation and deployment work.

Immediate plan:

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: 2026-09-07T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx rate from sentinel2b in production (us-west-2)

Jasmine / Evelyn — quick technical update from triage:

Summary (what we found):
- Root cause: a compilation-path race in a kernel selection code path for sentinel2b when a model shard is compiled on a GPU with an uncommon driver/kernel combo. This leads to sporadic KV-cache eviction during warmup which cascades into repeated 5xx/timeouts for in-flight requests.
- Scope: impacts sentinel2b instances launched since 2026-09-07 08:40 PDT in a subset of us-west-2 pools. Not all customers or routes are affected.
- Impact window: ~08:55–10:40 PDT.

Actions taken (completed):
1) At 10:05 PDT we flipped routing for LumenTech traffic from sentinel2b (latest) -> sentinel2b-v2-stable. This reduced error rate from ~8% -> ~0.3% within 8 minutes.
2) At 10:20 PDT we disabled the failing kernel selection path via an emergency runtime hotpatch to skip compilation on the problematic GPU-driver combos.
3) At 10:35 PDT we scaled an extra warm pool to reduce cold-starts and primed KV caches for previously affected machines.

Next steps (planned):
- We'll ship a permanent fix in the runtime to better gate kernel compilation and add a retry-safe cache eviction policy (PR targeted for 2026-09-09).
- Postmortem draft is available (postmortem-draft.docx) with full timeline, logs and suggested compensating controls.

Apologies for the outage. We're also proposing a one-time service credit for the impacted window; we'll follow up with account team to formalize.

Ben Carter
Incident Lead, Support Engineering
ben_carter@redwood.com

References: Jira INF-4372 (incident), Drive logs link provided in follow-up.

Subject: sentinel2b service degradation — summary & next steps

Hi Evelyn / LumenTech team —

Thank you again for your patience while we investigated the elevated 5xx/timeout errors you experienced on 2026-09-07. Below is a concise summary and the post-incident actions we're taking.

What happened (summary):
- Between ~08:55–10:40 PDT on 2026-09-07, a subset of sentinel2b instances in us-west-2 experienced a spike in 5xx responses caused by a kernel-selection/compilation race path that triggered unexpected KV-cache evictions during warmup.
- The issue only affected recently launched shards on a small set of GPU-driver combos.

Impact:
- LumenTech: automated smart-suggest/autocomplete endpoints saw increased error rates (~8% peak), with customer-facing timeouts reported for some users.
- Broader: small percentage of other hosted customers on sentinel2b in us-west-2 saw transient errors; most traffic was unaffected thanks to routing fallbacks.

Immediate mitigations completed:
- Traffic rerouted to sentinel2b-v2-stable for affected customers (completed 10:05 PDT).
- Emergency runtime hotpatch deployed to skip the problematic compilation path (completed 10:20 PDT).
- Added warm pool capacity and primed KV caches (completed 10:35 PDT).

Root cause and permanent fixes:
- Root cause: kernel selection bug leading to unsafe cache eviction during warmup.
- Permanent fix: change in runtime gating logic and safer cache eviction policy; PR and QA targeted for 2026-09-09 and staged deploy across regions the week of 2026-09-14.

Customer-facing remediation and credits: 
- We're proposing a one-time service credit for the impacted window. Monica (Customer Success) will follow up to formalize the credit and any follow-on support.

What we need from you:
- Please review the attached postmortem draft and the Drive logs (link below). If you have additional traces or requests, send them to ben_carter@redwood.com and me.

Links & artifacts:
- Postmortem draft: postmortem-draft.docx (attached)
- Logs and traces: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_example_logs
- Incident ticket: Jira INF-4372

We're available to review the postmortem with your engineering team if you'd like a live walkthrough. Again, apologies for the disruption — we're committed to preventing similar regressions.

Best regards,
Jasmine Liu
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
